stories.title: Michigan drivers to see lower fees for catastrophic coverage. How much?
stories.summary: Michigan drivers with catastrophic auto insurance coverage will see lower assessment fees starting next year due to auto insurance reforms. The Michigan Catastrophic Claims Association announced a $63 pure premium charge and $10 deficit recoupment charge for fiscal year 2027-28, down from current rates of $65 and $19. The reduction follows bipartisan auto no-fault legislation signed by Governor Gretchen Whitmer in 2019.

stories.title: Want in-flight Starlink? Expanded access coming from American Airlines
stories.summary: American Airlines will expand Starlink satellite Wi-Fi to its entire mainline fleet of over 1,000 aircraft starting in early 2027, building upon a previous announcement to add the service to 500 narrowbody planes. The airline, which operates through several Michigan airports including Detroit Metro, made the announcement in an Oct. 8 news release. SpaceX's Lauren Dreyer highlighted the service's fast, reliable internet for passengers during travel.

stories.title: PCEP Peer to Peer Program Promotes Inclusive Environment
stories.summary: The Peer to Peer Program at Plymouth Canton Education Park (PCEP) fosters inclusive connections between students with and without disabilities through collaborative activities like quizzes, music sessions, and social events. Led by Jacklyn Klotz and special education teachers, the program is recognized as an Evidence-Based Practice for students with disabilities and aims to expand with new initiatives like team games and entrepreneurship training.
entities: National Clearinghouse on Autism Evidence and Practice (NCAEP)

stories.title: Steward of Democracy
stories.summary: Michael Siegrist, a former Schoolcraft College alumnus and township clerk, emphasizes the integrity of the election system and was awarded Michigan Association of Municipal Clerks Township Clerk of the Year. He advocates for public involvement in election processes and is pursuing certifications to further his expertise in election administration.

stories.title: What is Columbus Day, Indigenous Peoples' Day? See debate
stories.summary: Columbus Day and Indigenous Peoples' Day both fall on Monday, Oct. 12, 2026, creating a scheduling conflict. While Columbus Day is recognized as a federal holiday, Indigenous Peoples' Day has gained traction as an alternative observance in some communities.

stories.title: Two Michigan tribes complete a 130-mile kayak voyage along Lake Michigan
stories.summary: Two Michigan tribes, the Nottawaseppi Huron Band of the Potawatomi and the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi, completed a 10-day, 130-mile kayak and canoe journey along Lake Michigan to reaffirm their ancestral friendship and connection to water. The 'Paddle to Pokagon' voyage, which began on October 3 and concluded on October 12 (Indigenous Peoples’ Day), included gatherings, cultural ceremonies, and environmental stewardship efforts. Tribal members emphasized the importance of preserving traditions and inspiring younger generations through ancestral waterways.
entities: Nottawaseppi Huron Band of the Potawatomi

photo.alt: Scenes from the 'Paddle to Pokagon' voyage, which reaffirms the longstanding friendship between the Nottawaseppi Huron Band and the Pokagon Band of Potawatomi in a traditional and sovereign way. (Photo/Skyla Jewell-Hammie)

stories.title: Livonia man who records conversations in public, posts them online pleads guilty to fleeing police
stories.summary: A Livonia man who used Meta glasses to record public conversations and post them online pleaded guilty in Wayne County to a charge of fleeing police. Charles TenBroeck, also known as Tom Rizz, admitted to disabling the recording light on his glasses and faced complaints from multiple individuals who felt uncomfortable with his actions. Despite legal concerns, police previously stated his actions did not meet criminal elements, but he now faces sentencing on December 9.

source.name: Erika Erickson, Kayla Clarke, Samantha Sayles

stories.title: $155M sports medicine complex planned at University of Michigan
stories.summary: The University of Michigan will likely approve construction on a $155 million sports medicine facility, with the UM Board of Regents set to vote on the project during their Oct. 15 meeting in Flint. Named for Nathan and Catherine Forbes, the Nathan and Catherine Forbes Sports Medicine Institute aims to open by fall 2028 and will span 100,000 square feet across three floors. The facility will include exam rooms, surgical centers, and advanced medical spaces, supported by donations from the Forbes couple and additional contributions from Bill and Sally Martin.

stories.title: Ann Arbor hospital earns national recognition for physician well-being
stories.summary: Trinity Health Ann Arbor and IHA Medical Group received silver-level recognition from the American Medical Association as a Joy in Medicine organization, highlighting their commitment to reducing physician burnout and supporting professional fulfillment. The health system is one of only eight in Michigan to earn the designation and the only one recognized alongside its integrated medical group. The AMA's program honors organizations that prioritize proven methods to reduce burnout and enhance professional satisfaction through documented efforts in commitment, assessment, leadership, and practice environment efficiency.

stories.title: Evacuation order lifted as work continues to contain Upper Peninsula wildfires
stories.summary: Firefighters report progress containing two wildfires in Marquette and Baraga counties after cooler temperatures and higher humidity reduced activity. Evacuation orders have been lifted, but residents are urged to remain prepared. The Ridge Fire (450 acres, 20% contained) and Craig Lake Fire (400 acres, 25% contained) were spotted by a DNR pilot on October 9. The Noquemanon Trail system and temporary flight restrictions remain in place.
